utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Registrar, please, could you call the case?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-74-T, the Prosecutor versus Prlic et al. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Registrar. This is Wednesday, September 17. I want to welcome the accused, the Defence counsels, Mr. Stringer and his colleagues, our witness, and everyone helping us around this courtroom. We'll now continue the cross-examination. I welcome Ms. Novica once again and I will give her the floor.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. Please look at 2D 01421. That was the document we looked at yesterday, just before breaking. For the sake of the transcript, let me state that at page 98, line 9, of yesterday's transcript, instead of the word "munare" used by the witness, which also means "minaret," it was interpreted as "well." So it should read "minaret." Witness, I hope you have found the document.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: This is a list or document of the Islamic community facilities destroyed during the war. This list was sent by the committee of the Islamic community of Mostar and it is signed by the chief imam of that community. Did you know the gentleman?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Very well. Yesterday, I wanted to ask you to look at all these buildings, namely, mosques and mesjids, which, according to this list sent to Bishop Peric in January 1993, damaged during the conflict with Serbs. Is that right? Does this correspond to what you remember of the period? This was something that was the subject of your study, was it not?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I am saying this for the benefit of Their Honours and everyone else, including the Prosecutors, that at the front of the binder that I prepared, you have an excerpt of the indictment, which I prepared for everyone. That's paragraph 116 of the indictment, and let me read the beginning of it: "During and within the siege of Eastern Mostar, the forces of Herceg-Bosna HVO have deliberately destroyed or heavily damaged the following mosques or places of worship in East Mostar." What follows is a list of roughly nine such buildings. I will be reading from the indictment, and you will try and identify, among the mosques or buildings in the list, the ones that you know of. The first one is Yavuz Selimov [as interpreted] Mosque, known as --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters note that we don't have the original of the indictment or the text of the indictment. It's very difficult to follow at this pace.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we do have this difficulty. I will have to give the list to the interpreters subsequently, and then we will have to correct the transcript. Otherwise, it's going to take up too much time.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Therefore, the Sultan Yavuz Selimova Mosque, from the indictment, can it be found under the list of mesjids?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And does it not say that the damage was major?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let us go on. Hadzi Mehmed-Beg Karadjozeva Mosque, Hadzi Mehmed-Beg Karadjozeva Mosque. Can you look at the list and more closely under number 2 of the list. Is that the same mosque?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let's go on. Koski Mehmed-Pasha Mosque. Please look under number 7 of the list of that particular document. Is that the same name of the mosque, but shortened?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Nesuh Aga Vucjakovic Mosque, Nesuh Aga Vucjakovic Mosque. Can you please look at number 3 on the list. Is that the same mosque?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Hadzi Ahmed Aga Lakisic Mosque -- Hadzi Ahmed Aga Lakisic Mosque. Witness, is that the mosque listed under number 14?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the shortened name of the same mosque.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note, can any of the extra microphones please be switched off.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The next one is Cosa Jahja -- I think my microphone is on. Is there a problem? Somebody's microphone was on? Let us repeat this last one. Cosa Jahja Hodza Mosque, also known as the Cosa Jahja Hodzina Mosque. Please look at the mesjid listed under number 2. Is that the same one? Under number 2, it says "Jahja Hodza," whereas what I read out was Cosa Jahja Hodza Mosque." Is that the same one? Or rather it's a mesjid, is it not?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It might well be, but --

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: What is it that confuses you there?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what I find confusing is that the list you're reading from, as well as on this particular list, very often what is used are both the names that are popularly used, used among the folk, and then officially used.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: But can you confirm for me that Cosa Jahja Hodza Mosque, or evidently a mesjid, something that is called Jahja Hodza Mesjid or Mosque popularly?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: We will not be focusing specifically on the official names, but just confirm for me whether the one that I'm reading does correspond to the one that is listed there under a colloquial, popular name, which was normally shortened, was it not?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let us go on. Hadji Kurta or Tabacica Mosque, and please direct your attention to number 6 on the list. Is that Kurtova Tabacica Mosque the same one as the one I've read out?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it's the same.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And finally Hadzi Memija Cernica Mosque, does it correspond to the mosque listed under number 5?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you confirm for me that you are fully in agreement with the letter sent by the Islamic Community of Mostar from January 1993, that the mosques were damaged, to a lesser or a greater degree, in Mostar during the conflict with the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can confirm that, yes, since the engineers of the enterprise for the construction and reconstruction made an assessment of the damage on these mosques, and they were, in fact, referenced in the book called "Urbicide."

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let us move on to another topic and another document, which is 2D 00017, so triple 0, 17, and you can find it right behind the document we've just been looking at in your binder. This is the decision of the Crisis Staff of the municipality of Mostar. This document was marked also as P 00170, and it was exhibited under both numbers. By way of a reminder of what I'm going to ask you about, this decision, under item 3, established the Croatian Defence Council, which consisted of members of Muslim and Croat peoples. Your answer to the question about the Muslim people was that they had a unit of their own which was called the Independent Battalion; is that right?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: You also told us how it came about that the Crisis Staff of the municipality ceased to operate, but let us briefly look at document 1D 1572, which was provided to everyone in the courtroom at a later date, so it was copied and distributed subsequently. This is a public rally of the fighters of the Independent Battalion of Mostar, held on the 12th of July, 1992. The document was published in the Mostar Jutro [phoen] publication. Are you aware of it being a bulletin or some sort of a publication of the Mostar Independent Battalion?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: In this first column, the seventh line of the second paragraph in English, I believe. The end of the second paragraph: "With the start of the fighting in the first skirmishes with a better-equipped and armed Chetnik units, what was noted was that the way the TO units had so far been organised was not suitable for that sort of warfare for such a rigid and ruthless war. The cooperation with HVO units at the beginning of the fighting caused the organisation of the unit to change, and on the 12th of April, 1992, the Independent Battalion of the defence of Mostar was established, which became part of the HVO forces." Mr. Puljic, this is fully consistent with what you've said, is it not?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The Independent Battalion itself says that upon its establishment, it became part of the HVO, did it not?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let us skip one paragraph and move on to the point where the Independent Battalion confirms its unity with the HVO, and it says: "Upon the loss of the left bank of the Neretva, the battalion consolidated its ranks and companies, composed of some 200 men, and upon the order of the Municipal Staff of the HVO, dated the 21st of May, they carried out tasks in the sector of Raska Gora until the 11th of June, where they demonstrated the -- an adequate level of organisation and combat readiness." Is that right?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: According to this, the Independent Battalion was formally part of the HVO, just as you said in item 3 of your decision, and this, in fact, proves that this was indeed the case during the fighting against the Serbs. Sir, do you know that the Independent Battalion, upon -- or, rather, when the Crisis Staff stopped functioning, continued to remain part of the HVO? What's more, they continued to rely on them for logistic support, in terms of material and technical equipment and so on?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that, and that's the truth.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Then we will cover the next document only cursorily. The first document is 2D 00522. Sir, we see a significant point here, and that's that it says in the heading: "Croatian Defence Council, Independent Battalion, Mostar defence"?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Somebody signed on behalf of Commander Arif Pasalic. You knew that Arif Pasalic was commander of that battalion, did you not?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: And it says: "Considering the fact that we have completely run out of ammunition, please provide us with the same so that we could continue executing combat activities." And he is addressing the Municipal Staff of the HVO on the 13th of July, 1992. Does this tally with your knowledge of how things worked?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And you can also look at the seal, which is quite interesting.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes. We have been analysing the seal previously, and we will continue to do so. There is quite a number of them. But I have a great many documents still to cover, and I have to do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Let us now look at the next document, that is 2D 00523. 2D 00523. Have you found it?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Again, you can see that it's the 1st Mostar Brigade, and we're talking about the transformation. It states the Command of the Mostar Brigade. The date is very interesting. That's the 31st of October, 1992. Again, it's a request for ammunition, supplies. It's again signed personally by the commander, Mr. Arif Pasalic. The seal is different, and it states: "HVO Mostar, County Headquarters, Logistics Department for Technical Services." Did you have information that this went on?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: We can see the document is from the month of October 1992?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did have that information.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: We're going to look at the last document because of the date. I picked several because of the date. That is 2D 524. This is signed by Commander Midhat Hujdur. You probably knew him or had heard of him.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had heard of him.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: To the municipal county headquarters on the 12th of December, 1992. This is a request for equipment and materiel; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Mr. Puljic, did you know that at the time you formed the Crisis Staff, at least two groups existed among the Muslims? I know that now they are called "Bosniaks," but that's what they were called then. So within the SDA, there was one group which took part in the participation of those documents, and there was another one which was in a way linked with the Islamic community. Did you know that they were opponents, that one group was in favour of the HVO and the other group was opposed to cooperation with HVO structures?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I knew about that.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now I'm going to ask you to look at another document, that is, 2D 00007. It's a document that I assume you haven't seen before, and perhaps you did. That is information about the situation and problems in Mostar and Herzegovina, dated September 1992, and it says that it was drafted by the Muslim Cultural Circle as part of the Islamic community; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you agree with me that that was precisely the group that was opposed to any kind of cooperation with the HVO?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Your Honours, I would like to ask you -- I would like to interrupt myself, because according to the calculations of the Registrar, which are absolutely correct, I have 25 minutes left for my cross. I would like, when this time runs out, to deduct the rest of the time from my time for my Defence, because perhaps I would like to have another ten minutes at the most to complete another two topics with this witness very briefly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam Nozica, the Trial Chamber said yesterday you had two hours for the entire Defence teams, and you were supposed to find an arrangement among yourselves, and you said that you did find an arrangement, and so that the three teams that would take the floor would use up these two hours. All we want is to make sure that the three Defence teams don't take more than two hours, because if we go beyond those two hours, then we're going to create a new problem, which will have consequences on further work. So it was up to you to find an arrangement with your colleagues.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We agreed. I am just waiting for this consultation. We agreed we all needed 45 minutes each. That's what we agreed on. I'm going to see, with my colleague Ms. Pinter, if they need all their time or if they could give us ten minutes. I didn't wish to go to the harm of anyone, so I thought perhaps I could be granted ten more of those minutes. Well, obviously they're not able to give me that time, so if you permit, I would like to take another ten minutes so that I could complete this topic. I would like to use my time for this; no other Defence. General Praljak's Defence has provided this time for me. All right, thank you. The general has decided I have ten minutes, so I can continue.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Since I have ten minutes, I would like to ask you very quickly to go through this document, only as much as your memory serves you. I'm going to ask you to look at the introductory part, and in the introductory part, look at the paragraph at the bottom. This is page 3 in the English. It says: "In the first days of the war, when there was fighting over the part of the city on the left bank of the Neretva River, the chairman of the regional board of the SDA announced publicly in the media that the TO units of the city of Mostar had been placed under the unified command of the HVO." And he says that decision, made by a small circle of people, had far-reaching consequences for Mostar and the region. Sir, this is an assessment of the document's drafters. From previous documents we were able to see that units under the control of the B and H Army, in December, two or three months after this writing, are still acting within the HVO and are asking it for logistical support or to provide them with weapons, and that is what the HVO did; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Now I'm going to ask you to look at -- we don't have time to look at anything else from this. Let's look at item 9 of this report. Please look at it. This is page 0017. 0017, its titled: "Finances," that section. In this part, he talks about the breakup of the financial system, the fact that the banks did not work anymore. In response to my learned friend Mr. Karnavas' question yesterday, you said that had -- the BH dinar or any other dinar that existed at the time was not physically able to reach your area from Sarajevo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I would now like you to look at the next page, that is, page 18, and it's under the heading: "Traffic." Can you confirm that in this report, the situation, as reported, was exceptionally difficult because of the destruction of the bridges, and that this part of the information provided is absolutely accurate? Well, you just follow what I have said. Is this stated here?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I think that the text here is accurate.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes, this is precisely what we want to see, that from the document which was drafted by the Cultural Circles, which are part of the Islamic community, affirms what you said yesterday. Can you look at the next page? This is PTT, and this is page 19 in the English, and that's where it is stated that the PTT traffic has stopped, and Mostar, as the main postal centre for the aforementioned areas, have ceased to operate. On the 29th of April, 1991, all financial flows via the PTT have stopped. Does that reflect the situation as you know it?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This is correct in view of the fact that the PTT was on the edge of the conflicts and people were killed.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter has missed the first part of the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: -- it is said here that -- we're talking about railway traffic here, and it is said that the damaged railway lines are there, and precisely because of that, the traffic -- the railway traffic is not proceeding and it has to be done in a combined way, using roads and trucks. Does that accord with what your information about what happened in 1992 with the railway traffic?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does. The traffic was not really possible to organise, even in a combined manner.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: At the end, we have a passage that is called: "Urban Planning and Reconstruction." In English, that is page 22, which talks precisely about what I asked you about the first time, how the Serbs in fact -- or the Greater Serbian ideology was destroying all the cultural facilities and urban centres that the Muslims had built over the centuries and gave them its specific outlook, and this, of course, includes the destruction of mosques and mesjids; can you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Can you now look at the one-but-last paragraph on the next page, and it says: "The failure to observe existing republican regulations with regard to abandoned flats and unauthorised activities in relation to these flats, may objectively result in major problems and tension. The destruction of immovable property is leading to a further reduction in housing units and business space, which are badly needed by the city and municipality." Mr. Puljic, from this document, which is written by the Cultural Circle as part of the Islamic community, precisely talks about what you talked about, that there was no -- or that the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina did not adopt regulations on abandoned apartments, and it is affirmed here that there was willful entry into these apartments, which created chaos in that situation. Is that something that accords with what you know?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does. There were people in the streets who had no roof over their heads, and there were empty apartments, but at the same time I said that the municipal services that were supposed to apply these regulations absolutely and completely had fallen apart at that point in time, which means had you even wanted to apply any regulations, you were unable to do so because there were no desk officers or there was no personnel who could establish, during that time, which apartment was empty, who could issue a decision and make it possible for somebody to move in there.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, this circle here that is part of the Islamic community complains about the lack of regulations of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina which did not, by September, regulate this sphere; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Well, we are going to move to our last document. I'm going to finish here. I would like you to look at document in my binder that is 2D 1420, and we don't have enough time so let us finish with that document. Have you looked at this document? It's the last document in my binder, a document to the 4th Corps of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina? That's what it says, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: All right. Very well. Let's see what this is. It's a document -- it's a report of the 3rd of March, 1993, which is submitted by the deputy commander for legal affairs, Mr. Temin Semir, and it is being sent to the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina, 4th Corps, and it says: "In order to consider jurisdictional regulation of life and employment, for the members of the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, we are submitting to you reports on the activity of the Legal Department of the 1st Mostar Brigade." Article 2 talks about the activities over the past period, and they talk about housing problems. I cannot manage to read everything. I just would like to draw your attention to specific points here. Under 3, it talks about problems in work, and then it says: "Relations with the HVO." And then under 2: "Non-functioning of civilian authorities," and this is something that you talked about. We're talking about the territory under the control of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina in March, and that is what they thought was their territory. No army legal activities. They are talking about the usurpation of the military housing stocks by the HVO. First let me ask you this: What they're saying here, there is no civilian authority, no judicial bodies, and there are no Official Gazettes, directives and so on, does that correspond with what you know? Let me first ask you that.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As of the 30th of March, 1993, there were civilian organs.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: I'm talking about the area under the control of the Army of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I absolutely agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Yes, yes, please concentrate.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I absolutely agree with you.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So it says here usurpation of the military housing stock of the HVO. Didn't we see yesterday that the HVO of the municipality or the civilian authorities in Mostar did allocate military apartments to members of the Muslim ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: We saw that yesterday in the document, and this was something that Mr. Karnavas asked you about. Now let's move to item 4. There is one thing we have, and that is very important. What was specifically done to resolve the status of fighters? Salaries distributed for December and January in DM. Please, Mr. Puljic, it follows from this document that the army, also the armija, received salaries in DM?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: The document is of the 3rd of March, 1993. Can you please tell the Trial Chamber what the reason for this was? Was any money able to reach Mostar in any other way, any possible way?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: So you agree with me that members of the armija and all citizens in Mostar at that point in time were using German marks?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And now for the transcript, we saw yesterday that Majda Cupina was given a military apartment on the 16th of September, 1992, and this was noted in document 1D 00641. Thank you very much, sir, for your replies.

utterances.speaker: MS. NOZICA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you to Your Honours. I have finished with my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Mr. Praljak's Defence team now.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning to everyone in the courtroom. Let me immediately take up on what my colleague Nozica was just discussing, so I'll rearrange my plan a bit. Can the witness be handed -- yes, right, the book. And can we call up document 3D 010207. This part of my cross-examination has to do with the document that the Defence for Dr. Prlic used in direct. That's 1D 02647. At the same time, it also takes the examination from the point where Ms. Nozica stopped.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Please look at the large book you have in front of you. Their Honours and the Prosecution have the printed version of the book in e-court. First of all, are you familiar with the company called Urbin?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It was the name that was given to the public enterprise for the construction and reconstruction in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Do you mean that it's the legal successor of that company?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It's just that the company at some point changed its name.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: My colleague Kovacic tells me to repeat the number of the document the Prlic Defence used. This is 1D 02647, and the document of the Defence of General Praljak is 3D 01027. Mr. Puljic, are you familiar with Staka Matkovic?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Who is she?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: She is an employee in the housing department of the public enterprise for the construction and reconstruction in Mostar, which was subsequently renamed Urbin.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Very well. Now please can you flip through the book now and look at some of the pages that are more legible, and then you'll see in the top left-hand corner a heading which says: "Public Enterprise for the Construction and Reconstruction of Mostar." This confirms that the documents were produced by that public company in September 1992; is that right, because we have the date on the right-hand side?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: What does this book represent?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The book is the basic document, a book of records of all the socially-owned flats in the municipality of Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: If one were to make certain analyses on the basis of this book, the analysis would be based on facts that were ascertained at the time the data was collected. The data contained in the book can be considered reliable, can it not?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. All the data contained in this book can be considered reliable.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. Yesterday, during the examination-in-chief and in response to His Honour Judge Antonetti's question, you gave an answer that I believe needs clarification. When we're talking about the protection of the old bridge, and I'm referring to document of the Prlic Defence 1D 02644, who was it who physically placed the board work on the bridge, including the rubber?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the HVO engineering troops.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: At page 61 of yesterday's transcript, it followed from the question put by His Honour Judge Antonetti that these were the employees of the public enterprise for the construction and reconstruction of Mostar who did that. You're saying it wasn't them, that it was in fact the HVO engineering troops?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When we're talking about the physical works on the site, it was done by the HVO engineering troops.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Do you know who it was who ordered that this job be done in the HVO?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who gave the order. I know who executed the task.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Do you know the name Ljubo Peric?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Who was he?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He discharged certain jobs in the logistics at the time.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can the question please be repeated, and can, please, the speakers break between question and answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And all this because I'm rushing to save time. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Mr. Puljic, tell me, who was it who provided the planks, the rubber material and everything else that was needed for the protection of the bridge?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was the HVO engineering troops.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Mr. Kovacic told me to repeat my previous question, who was Mr. Anto Ivankovic, but because I was rushing, it was not recorded in the transcript. Do you know Mr. Ivankovic? I was waiting for the transcript to appear. Can you please repeat your answer?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do know Mr. Anto Ivankovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday, you were shown 1D 01804. It discusses the establishment of the public company of Elektroprivreda of the Community of Herceg-Bosna. Do you recall this? There's no need for us to look at the document now?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Before the public company of Elektroprivreda of Herceg-Bosna came into existence, another company was active in Herceg-Bosna. Do you know the name of it? It was Elektrohercegovina, was it not?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Do you know who the manager of Elektrohercegovina was?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Can I assist you? Edin Omeragic?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Omeragic. Do you know the gentleman? I don't mean personally, but did you hear of him?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know him personally, too. I know Mr. Edin Omeragic personally.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Thank you. Document 1D 01987 is the document the Defence for Mr. Prlic used, and this is a report on the activities of the European Community and Observers and UNPROFOR in Mostar, and up until they left Mostar. And I will ask Their Honours to allow General Praljak to put questions in relation to this document, and I kindly ask you to take that document, because you'll be needing it. And while you're doing that, please focus on the following dates: The 3rd of May, 1992, and that's 1D 01987. The date is the 3rd of May, 1992, the 6th of May, 1992 - that's page 10 in Croatian - 12 and 14, all in the Croatian version. Under those dates, General Praljak is mentioned. Do you know if General Praljak was in the area of Mostar, and I'm talking about mid-1992, the months of May and June?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about him.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: But you didn't see him at the time?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Did you know or did you hear who was it who was in command of the liberation of the left bank of Mostar, the so-called [indiscernible]?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my knowledge, it was General Praljak.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. My part of the cross-examination is finished, Your Honours, and now I will give the floor to General Praljak to do -- to examine on the matters he, himself, participated in. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Good morning, Your Honours. Good morning, Witness. How much time do I have left, please, so that I know how to organise myself?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 4D had 42 minutes, 2D had 39 minutes -- rather, 50 minutes, so you had 30 minutes left, at most, for you. Mrs. Pinter must have used some 10 to 15 minutes, so you must have 15 minutes left, I think. Cross-examination by Accused Praljak:

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Please look for document 1D 01567. 1D 01567. That's a document that Mr. Karnavas had in his binder, and it concerns water. While you're looking for it, can I ask that this piece of paper be placed on the ELMO. It's a small diagram. Mr. Puljic, 1D 01567. We'll only be looking at two documents on the issue of water. Have you found the document?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] 1567. Can he please be assisted in finding the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Oh, it isn't there?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: You have it on the screen, then. It's the 14th of September, 1993. Marko Vidacek signed the document. Do you know him?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: The document clearly describes -- or, rather, describes all the problems concerning water in 1993 in clear terms. Look at the first -- second paragraph, which says -- or rather, fourth paragraph: "Because of damages caused by shelling of Studenac water source in May 1992 ..." First of all, did you know that in May 1992, the Studenac and Radobolja water sources were badly damaged by shelling?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Thank you. In view of the damage inflicted on Mostar over the months that it was shelled, the months of April, May and June, did hundreds, thousands, or tens of thousands of shells land on Mostar?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tens of thousands of shells.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Were there children killed in the shelling?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Excuse me, Witness. How do you know this? How can you affirm that it's tens of thousands? Where did you get this figure?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] General Praljak offered me three possibilities. Had he said one hundred -- hundreds of thousands, or 200.000, I would have confirmed that, because a shell landed every second and one could hear that. I could say that it was shelling with countless shells, or with no beginning or end, and with no evident purpose. You could never tell when the next shell would land.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: So it is more or less guesswork? You do not have -- you have never seen any statistics or anything like that, it's just your impression, which is, I mean, okay. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Your Honour, Judge Trechsel --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I asked a question of the witness, and the witness should answer it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, let me try. If we say that, on average, there was one shell landing every five minutes, then you have to count how many five minutes you have in a day, and then you count the days and you'll get to the number. But if you gave me any three figures, I'd always opt for the highest. But we could eventually arrive at a number. Of course, it would be an approximation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you. I think that's enough. Please, Mr. Praljak, continue. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: I invoked a very simple example. You gave us statistics of the destruction in the town. Can a tank shell destroy a mosque? And I'm asking you to respond from your expertise as an architect.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, not very likely, but it could.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: So from the extent of the damage, one could easily arrive at the number of shells that caused the damage in the first place?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Very well. In this document -- or, rather, first look at the diagram that I've drawn. It's on the ELMO. Is that an accurate picture of the situation in and outside Mostar, the position of the Radobolja and Studenac water sources, the lines -- the water lines as they ran?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Did both water lines from East Mostar pass across the bridges?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: When the bridges were destroyed, so were the water pipes supplying water to East Mostar, were they not?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Could the Radobolja water source, due to the law of communicating vessels, reach only the fourth floor of the buildings in Mostar?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Was the Studenac water source on the zero level and could only pump water when electricity was provided to the strength of 300 kilowatts?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, electricity was a precondition for the Studenac water source to provide water.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: In other words, no electricity, no --

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Water.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Above the fourth floor, the buildings had -- if they had more than four floors, then they had to have their own pumps, did they not?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Because of the shortage of time, I'm unable to cover everything I wanted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I'm looking at the drawing by Mr. Praljak. We can see both sources. We can see the supply of East Mostar passing through West Mostar, and we can see that if both bridges were destroyed, of course, the water supply could not reach the other side. However, the Studenac source passes through a bridge as well. Was that bridge destroyed or not? The Zeljeznicki Most bridge, yes, was it destroyed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. The railway bridge was also destroyed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Which means that if the three bridges were destroyed, there was no water supply anymore for East Mostar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] .

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Please look at 1D 01568. That's the next document we're looking at. You have it on the screen. Do you know Messrs. Vidacek and Vucic?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, both of them.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: The same issues are mentioned in this document. What is talked about, who should buy what from whom and who should buy the electrical cables so that the water can be pumped from the Studenac water source. Were you aware of the fact that there was no electricity at the Studenac source because the power lines were down and the transformer station could not be relied upon?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Can we now look at document 1D 1987, specifically page 17. I think that there was a confusion, perhaps caused by His Honour Judge Antonetti. When we were talking about the international organisation that wanted to bring women and children out of Mostar, it was referred to as the UNHCR.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Was it the UNHCR or the UNPROFOR that we were talking about at that time?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: All right. Well, it does say here what that was. Please, when the attempt was made -- first of all, tell me, in Mostar, when these meetings were held, Topic, Jaganjac, myself, would it be found out quickly, what we talked about? It would be known all over Mostar very quickly?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it would. Everything in Mostar is found out very quickly.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: When the first attempt was made by UNPROFOR to evacuate those women and children, what was the only road that they could use to leave the city?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The one and only road --

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Through Goranci?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Through Goranci.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Somebody who was going along the road via Goranci -- well, you said "through Goranci"?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: That road and the person or those moving on that road, were they subject to Serbian artillery?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and people were killed on that road.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: People were killed on that road. The first time when the UNPROFOR attempted to organise this evacuation, was this road shelled and the women and children were prevented from leaving?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that first attempt, but that road was always under fire from Serb positions.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Are you aware, as it is stated here -- can you look at the end of page 17? Are you aware that Mr. Lundgren suggested that the HVO leaves the left bank and leaves it to the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you please repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Are you aware that Mr. Lundgren suggested to the HVO, after making an agreement with Perisic and that team over there, that the HVO should leave the left bank of the Neretva and cede it to the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall that. It's possible, it's possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Please, can you now look at the paragraph on page 18, at the bottom of that page. Mr. Lundgren says that he was conveying the position of the Serb side or is conveying "our position" about the request of the JNA to be in charge of the left bank was not acceptable because the JNA was not a representative of the state, and "our position is that the people should be escorted to the Montenegro." Is it true that it was our position that Mostar should not be divided at any cost?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this position is familiar to me, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: And, finally, I have a few minutes left. Mr. Lundgren says towards the end that he had come with the wish to pull out the civilians and the wounded and to bring the Serb families to the right bank. Are you aware that the request of the Serb side was for the UNPROFOR to bring out Serb civilians to the left bank from the right bank?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Just -- just a couple of minutes more. At the time, were the Serbs at Hum and at Orlovac?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: And did they control completely the electrical facilities and transmission station at Cule?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Are you aware or do you know how much, at that point in time, if it was shut down in the proper way, as French experts recommended that to Mijo Brajkovic, what was the value of aluminium in dollars? How many hundreds of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I have a follow-up or, rather, a question to what you have answered right now. The question started with: "At the time." "At the time, were the Serbs at Hum," and so forth. What time did you refer to in your answer, at what time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: May 1992. And that was also the time you had in mind, Mr. Praljak? Okay, thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In response to your question, I don't know how much the aluminium enterprise would be worth in dollars, but I know that 5.000 people are making a living there, and indirectly, 20.000 people or more depend on it for their living. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: So the aluminium enterprise, if its furnaces were not shut down according to an exact procedure, and all of that -- and if this is not done, would this be completely destroyed, all the installations, without any chance of repair?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in that case the Mostar enterprise would have the same fate as the Sibenik one which has not been able to be repaired to date.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Meaning that you would need hundreds of millions of dollars to clear this ground and start all over from scratch?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Are you aware, in which way did the HVO make it possible for electricity to be --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Witness, what is your experience in the cost of cleaning up the land of a former aluminium factory? Why can you affirm that it costs hundreds and hundreds of millions of dollars? How many hundreds, and on what basis do you affirm that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't mention a single figure in relation to the value of aluminium or these costs. All I know is that it would be much more expensive to repair the factory than to build a new one. You would need to clear the ecological issues created by the old factory first, because if the aluminium enterprises were shut down incorrectly, you would be creating an ecological problem that would need to be resolved before a new factory could be built in its place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Thank you. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Your Honour Judge Trechsel, this is the case of another aluminium factory in Croatia, so these figures just seemed realistic when we were talking about the rebuilding of that plant, so it seemed a bit realistic if we applied it to this example too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but this is not correct, because now you were giving testimony, and that's not your task. You can only ask questions. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] I did put the question, and the witness did answer it. Well, this is the information that appeared in newspapers, so I thought that the gentleman would be aware of it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: And, please, can you please just tell me this: Well, I'm going to stop. Well, can you please look at this sketch that I made, to look at east and west, if that is correct. I marked only two bridges over the Drina. You know how many exactly there were, and you said who destroyed them. Are they --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction, over the Neretva River, not the Drina. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] ... and if you agree with the accuracy of the sketch, can you please sign the sketch, and also can you please answer the question about the effort put in by the HVO to bring electricity or restore electricity to the factory so that the aluminium complex could be shut down in the proper way to preserve the installations, in view of the fact that the Serbs were in charge of the Cule and Rastani power stations? If you don't know, you can just tell us.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I do know, because you can see on the basis of all the negotiations that there were constant attempts by the HVO to keep the Cule power station working, and that power plant was -- from Mr. Filipovic's report, you can see the efforts invested by the HVO to preserve the Cule power station and its operation. When this power station stopped working, the aluminium complex also stopped working, and it would not be shut down in the proper way, but it would be shut down improperly, and that would mean that it would be impossible to repair the aluminium complex. It was not then shut down, but would -- and it would be impossible to repair. This is something that I know well because it's just how things are.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the transcript does not seem to be reflecting that there's anything happening. Oh. Okay, now it's moving ahead, so I'm sure the gentleman is typing away. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PINTER
utterances.text: Are you aware that in May, and the date is mentioned in the report, a representative of the UNPROFOR was killed by the Serbs near the Cule power transmission station? Actually, he was a European observer.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am aware of that. That was the same day when the brother of one of my engineers was seriously wounded. THE ACCUSED PRALJAK: [Interpretation] Sir, thank you for your answers, and I thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We will have a break in a few minutes, and Mr. Stringer can start his cross-examination after the break. But I have one question for you. It's in line with the questions that were put to you yesterday. Yesterday, there was mention of three levels of power: the federal power, the power at the level of the republic and the power at the municipal level. I'm sure each and every one understood how things worked before the independence, independence which occurred in March 1992. Now, regarding federal power, I would like to know whether before March 1992, before the declaration of independence, federal -- I want to know whether federal authorities had any representatives in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Before I answer this question, I need to inform the Chamber that the answer to this question belongs to the general knowledge category, which can be correct or incorrect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, very well. Now, let's stay in your area of competence, in architecture. I would like to know whether you had a counterpart that was reporting to the federal authorities, as far as your area of competence is concerned, before March 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As for urbanism and construction, the local municipal authority had no links with the federal authorities in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, thank you. This is crystal clear. Now, at the level of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, I would like to know whether in the area of urbanism they had a person or representative in Mostar, or whether there was just no one because this was only under the competence of municipal authorities.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The municipality was exclusively in charge with that, but it had a strong communication or link with the ministry in Sarajevo, and that means that besides being responsible for our work to the municipality or the Municipal Assembly under regulations, we were also responsible to the ministry in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And the ministry at Sarajevo, but that means that there was no one in Mostar, in the city of Mostar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. You answered my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, although Mr. Praljak did say it, but the transcript did not register it. Mr. Praljak did ask for an exhibit number for the sketch that the witness signed and placed a date on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Let's have an IC number, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, the sketch shall be given Exhibit number IC 00843. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. We'll have a 20-minute break, and Mr. Stringer can get ready for the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Court is back in session. Mr. Stringer, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Mr. President, Your Honours, my colleague Kimberly West will be conducting the cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, Your Honours, everyone in the courtroom. Kim West for the Office of the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness. Now, you indicated that you were on the Crisis Staff for the Mostar Assembly; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And that in December of 1990, there had been elections for the Mostar Assembly?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which year was that?

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: If I can have a moment, Mr. President. I'm not getting the translation. Let me try this again.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, you indicated that you had been a member of the Crisis Staff in the Mostar Assembly; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And you know that in December of 1990, there had been elections for the Mostar Assembly?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: However, you did not run for one of those places, did you?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you. You ultimately became a member by virtue of your position; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have never been an assemblyman. I was a member of the Executive Board and the secretary of the Secretariat for Urbanism, Construction and Housing Affairs. However, by law and ex officio, I was duty-bound to attend Assembly meetings.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Nonetheless, sir, you were a member of the HDZ Party, were you not?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And when did you originally join?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A month or two -- or, rather, before the multiparty elections. I don't know the precise date.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: So in 1991, you were a member of the HDZ Party?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Now, I'm going to show you P 00302, and that's in the binder in front of you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Which one?

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: P 00302, the first binder.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Sir, do you have the B/C/S in front of you?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Now, this is dated 18 November 1991; correct? And if you just turn to the second page, you'll see that date.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And this is the document that established Herceg-Bosna; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, while it may be that it's 18 November 1991, if you look at the preamble, it's 3 July 1992 it was amended. So if we are going to be referring to documents and specifically pointing to dates, I would ask my colleague to be very precise.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: May I proceed, Mr. President? This document --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: May I have a ruling? May I have a ruling because the document is 3 July 1992. Now, if my colleague doesn't understand the significance, then it can be pointed out to her, but the document was amended. So if the purpose is to go back to 18 November, when in fact we're talking about 3 July 1992, there is a vast difference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. West, dates are extremely important, so please try to be -- try to ask the witness to specify the date. It may look pointless at first, but it could have an impact in the end, so please, if necessary, you know, ask the witness to help you to specify the date.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I'll do so.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: You indicated that this was the decision on establishing the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna; right? You understand that to be that decision?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but the dates confuse me.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Sir, let me ask you another question. Who signed this document?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Excuse me, you're correct, but whose name is at the bottom of the second page of this document?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mate Boban.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And Mr. Boban was the president of the -- or he established himself as the president of HZ-HB; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: To the left of that name, there is a date, right, right after "Mostar"?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: What does that date say?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "18 November 1991."

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Now, if we go back to the first page, under number 1, entitled "Reasons," it's this part where it's established what are the necessary purposes of establishing the community; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: So I'm going to read to you the second paragraph. It says: "Through their party, the Croatian Democratic Union, and through the legally-elected bodies of authority in this republic, Croats in Bosnia and Herzegovina have supported a sovereign Bosnia-Herzegovina but always emphasised that in so doing, they are protecting their own historical territories and the interests of the entire Croatian people." Do you see that part of it?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Now, you would agree with me that it appears that this language puts the focus on the Croat people and not any other ethnicity; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This refers to all the ethnic communities in Bosnia-Herzegovina, because it says: "... the Croats in Bosnia-Herzegovina, through their party and through the legally-elected bodies in this republic," and as soon as they are in favour of a sovereign Bosnia-Herzegovina, in my view, since they are in favour of a sovereign Herzegovina, they are in favour of there being all the national communities.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Sir, I see where you're pointing to at the beginning of that sentence, but if you focus on the part that says -- after "emphasised," it says: "... but always emphasised that in so doing, they are protecting their historical territories in the interests of the entire Croatian people." That does not include the Muslim people, nor the Serb people; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the second part of the sentence, the other peoples are not mentioned, indeed. However, the first part of the sentence says that they have supported a sovereign Bosnia-Herzegovina, and Bosnia-Herzegovina is the country of all its peoples.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Mr. Puljic, the day before yesterday, Judge Antonetti asked you a question on this very issue, and at that time he asked you: "When the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna was created, do you think that it was envisaged that within that community there would also be Muslims?" And your answer was: "In my view, yes. That is what I sensed -- I mean, how I felt. That would include all the people who wished to live in peace." And then a little bit later on at page 62 at the bottom, you say: "I'm talking about all the people who lived there, regardless of their ethnicity." Do you remember that testimony?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And in order to help us answer Judge Antonetti's question regarding whether Herceg-Bosna actually envisioned all ethnicities in it, I'd like to look at another document, and this is P 00071.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: Excuse me, Ms. West. Is it in binder 1?

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: It is. Thank you, Your Honour. Sir, it's also on the screen in front of you.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Do you see on top it's dated 12 November 1991; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: This is just within one week of the 18th. Now, in this document, it shows you conclusions from a meeting of the HDZ that was held in Grude one week before the 18th, and I want to see if it's consistent with your view at the time. If we look at the first paragraph, it's number 1, and towards the end of that paragraph it says that: "These two regional communities," meaning the Herzegovina Regional Community and the Travnik Regional Community, "these two regional communities have jointly and unanimously decided that the Croatian people in Bosnia-Herzegovina must finally carry out a decisive and active policy which would lead to the realisation of our centuries-old dream, a joint Croatian state." Now, you would agree with me that this proclamation -- or this sentence, rather, doesn't mention Muslims in it, does it?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Before I answer your question, I have to say that this is the first time I'm hearing of the existence of some Herzegovina Regional Community or Travnik Regional Community.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Okay. And my question is whether what I just read you mentions other ethnic groups besides Croats.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In what is today the Republic of Croatia, all peoples live together, just as was the case in Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And, again, my question for you is whether, in that sentence, there's any mention of any other ethnicity other than the Croats. Can you answer my question?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, my interpretation of certain texts is my personal matter. My opinion on a matter is personal. The one who authored the text should respond to your question of what was meant by that particular sentence.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Sir, that may be the case, but I'm asking you, and so do I take it that you cannot answer that question?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only the author of the text can answer this question, and this is some meaningless institution, the name of which I've just learnt now, one which didn't play any role at the time. This is the first time I hear of the existence of the Herzegovina Regional Community, of there having been such a community. I really don't know what the individuals who were part of it did or thought.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Okay. So let's just go a little bit further, and we'll try again. I'm going to the second paragraph --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this point I'm going to ask that a foundation be laid in order for the gentleman to answer these questions. She referred to -- I mean, the Prosecution referred to a question that was posed by you, President Antonetti. It called for his opinion. He gave the opinion. Now, what is in this document is irrelevant as to what was his opinion at the time, particularly given his answers that he was not at the meeting and he cannot answer the question. Now, the document stands on its own and we can all read it, but I don't think that she has laid a foundation upon which he can now, then, answer these questions. I would like a ruling on this.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Mr. President, may I be heard?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you. Two things. The first is the witness has already indicated that he was a member of the HDZ at this period of time. This is the biggest political issue going on, so I think he certainly has a position -- is in a position to share with us his thoughts. The second thing is I would recall the Chamber to Mr. Karnavas' direct testimony with this witness in which he went over a series of meetings with the UNPROFOR and ECMM, where the witness indicated, and I believe it was four meetings, that he was not even there. However, he gave us our -- his views of what they were thinking at the time. So I think I'm in a far better position to get his views on this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: First of all, being a member of a political party does not necessarily mean that you know everything that is going on in the party throughout the entire country. One can be a Democrat, and that doesn't necessarily mean that they know what Obama is doing at this particular moment, or Hilary Clinton, for that matter. That's number 1. Number 2, with respect to the gentleman's testimony to meetings with UNPROFOR and ECMM, let's keep in mind that this was about Mostar and where he was. His entire testimony deals with Mostar municipality, primarily Mostar city, for a very discrete period of time. Now, if a foundation can be laid that the gentleman was in a party leadership, that he was a member of the board of HDZ and thus was required to attend certain meetings or was being briefed, if he travelled to such conventions or meetings, then fine. But until such foundation is laid, simply being a member of a political party doesn't necessarily mean that you know the ins and outs of the party's activities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. West, the person does not know the document because obviously Travnik is not in his area of competence. However, contrary to what Mr. Karnavas is saying, as a member of the HDZ, he may have some inkling of political knowledge, and I believe that you may ask the question. But don't linger on this document too long. This -- you're not here to highlight the document, but only part of this document, if I've -- I believe that what you want to highlight is only part of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: I would like only to add to what has been said by Presiding Judge Antonetti the following, that, of course, the question is about the authenticity of the document and if it was a kind of only regional one, the document, or something more. Now, I just had a look at the signatories of the document, which is attached to the Croatian text of that regulation, position, and here it is handwritten page, and I found some well-known names, like "Dario Kordic, Zeljko Raguz, Milivoj Gagro" and others. Of course, I cannot read -- I should not read everything, but you may check yourselves, and which shows to me, at least, that it is not a Travnik document, so to say, but a document which was adopted by those people who participated at the given meeting in Travnik. So thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you, Judge Prandler.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Judge Prandler is perfectly right. Moreover, in the list, and I hadn't noticed this, in the list Mr. Topic is also indicated as having been there. Since Mr. Topic played a role in the Mostar municipality, since he is the vice-president of the HDZ, and that the witness is also a member of the HDZ, maybe Mr. Topic, on his way back from Travnik, had the opportunity to tell the members of the HDZ what happened. So this is the foundation. So please put your question, and let's see if you get what you want.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Now, sir, we'll go back to the first page of this document, under number 1, the second paragraph: "In order for this historical goal to soon become a reality, these two regional communities request the commencement of activities to formulate and issue legal and political documents, the proclamation of a Croatian banovina in BH, a referendum on accession of the Republic of Croatia." I'm going to stop right there. You see the term "Croatian banovina." Can you tell us what your understanding is of that?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only tell you as much as I was able to learn about the Croatian banovina, just as everybody else, from the history books.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And please tell us what that is.

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a territory that was set up in 1939 within the process of reorganisation of Yugoslavia, based on an agreement reached by the Yugoslav politicians.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Thank you. And it further says: "A referendum on accession to the Republic of Croatia." Now, you understand that to mean potentially joining the Republic of Croatia; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Based on what, Your Honour? Based on what is this assumption being made? Where is the foundation? And again I go back to my earlier question. Even Judge Prandler said, "Okay, we see some names," but where is the foundation that the gentleman was there or, as you noted, Judge Antonetti, that he was briefed thereafter in order for him to be able to answer these questions, and now the question assumes a fact that's not in evidence. So let's go step by step. Lay the foundation -- but look at the question, Your Honour. It's highly potent. I mean, to get a "yes" or "no" to that answer is irrelevant without laying the foundation.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Your Honour, my question, page 45, number 4, I just read the sentence, and my question to him was what was his understanding of that language, and he can answer he doesn't understand it --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, you understand that to mean. She is forcing the answer of what he understands that to mean, as opposed to, "What did you understand that to mean?" There is a distinction. I go back. Let's lay a foundation. Was he there, was he briefed, was he aware of this discussion, and only then should he be allowed to be given an opportunity to answer those questions that she wishes to answer -- him to answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Madam West, I thought I had been clear enough. First you should have asked the witness if Mr. Topic, on his way back from the meeting, had mentioned what happened to a certain number of people. He could have said "yes" or "no." If he says, "Yes," then you may ask him if they mentioned the issue of the banovina, if they mentioned a possible referendum. If he says, "No, no, we weren't briefed," well, then you continue and say, "Fine, but as a member of the HDZ, within your own party, were such issues discussed?"

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: Sir, you indicated that you had been a member of the HDZ through 1991; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
utterances.text: And you know that the issue of establishing a community for Herceg-Bosna was something that was discussed among the members; correct?

utterances.speaker: BORISLAV PULJIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're mentioning Herceg-Bosna now. The document doesn't mention Herceg-Bosna anywhere.

utterances.speaker: MS. WEST
